relations.subject: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
relations.evidence: His father, Gangadhar Tilak was a school teacher and a Sanskrit scholar who died when Tilak was sixteen.

relations.subject: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
relations.evidence: Tilak obtained his B.A. in Mathematics from the Deccan College of Poona in 1877.

relations.subject: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
relations.evidence: In 1879, he obtained his L.L.B degree from Government Law College.

relations.subject: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
relations.evidence: Inspired by Vishnushastri Chiplunkar, he co-founded the New English school for secondary education in 1880 with a few of his college friends, including Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, Mahadev Ballal Namjoshi and Vishnushastri Chiplunkar.

relations.subject: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
relations.evidence: The success of the school led them to set up the Deccan Education Society in 1884

relations.subject: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
relations.evidence: The Society established the Fergusson College in 1885 for post-secondary studies. Tilak taught mathematics at Fergusson College. In 1890, Tilak left the Deccan Education Society for more openly political work.
